newsitem.title: QATAR: U.S. Enron shifts focus to India from Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Enron shifts focus to India from Israel.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Enron Corp has turned its eye away from Israel as a significant market for its gas "in the immediate term" but will keep the door open for future negotiations, an Enron official said on Wednesday.

"Our main focus is now on the Indian market which, we think, can absorb large amounts of gas," Kelly Kimberly, spokeswoman of the Houston-based corporation, told Reuters on the sidelines of a gas conference in the Qatari capital Doha.

Enron signed a letter of intent with Israel in October 1995 to supply two million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from 2001. But citing a lack of progress in negotiations to translate the intent into a firm sales-and-purchase agreement, Tel Aviv shelved the deal last November.
Israel's oil ministry said it was cheaper to buy piped gas from neighbouring Egypt and former Soviet countries than to import LNG on tankers via the Gulf and the Red Sea to Israel.
Kimberly said: "We are keeping our doors open, but in the immediate term we have shifted our focus."
"There is a lot of interest in India and we have signed memoranda of understanding with various state agencies to supply our gas in India," she said.
Enron is negotiating a joint venture deal with the state's Qatar General Petroleum Corporation to set up a $5 billion project to produce five million tonnes of LNG annually.

Kimberly said two million tonnes of the planned output would go to fuel a 2,500-megawatt power plant it is building at Dabhol in the western Indian state of Maharashtra and one million tonnes annually to Gujarat Gas Corporation, with which it has signed a memorandum of understanding.
"The rest could be supplied to other state agencies with whom we have been holding discussions or signed accords," she said, adding: "We are quite optimistic."
On Tuesday, the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu announced that it had awarded a multi-million-dollar contract to Enron to build a 242-megawatt power plant in the state.
